_source: ArgoUML Cookbook in the same revision (trunk@13713, documentation/cookbook: subsystems.xml, inside_subsystems.xml, subsystem*.xml). Purpose and layer statements restated close to verbatim; package and class names removed so that hidden runs get no path back. Written and frozen before any ArgoUML run. Modules without a cookbook section get only what the cookbook says of them.
application: Application, the top level subsystem: provides the entry point when starting ArgoUML (it contains the main method) and starts the ball rolling; it initialises the other subsystems and depends on them, but no other subsystem depends on it
diagrams: Diagrams, a View subsystem: presents the diagrams to the user and lets the user manipulate them through the view; its classes extend the graph editing framework's base classes (graph models, figures, selections), and it depends on the Model and the GUI
notation: Notation, a View and Control subsystem: generates, updates and edits, in different languages, the textual representation of one or more UML model elements, attached e.g. to a diagram figure or an explorer entry
explorer: Explorer (formerly the Navigator), a View and Control subsystem: provides tree views of the model elements, diagrams and other objects, with configurable perspectives
codeGeneration: Code Generation, a Control subsystem: the point where the different languages register that they can generate code, and the functions common to all languages
reverseEngineering: Reverse Engineering, a Control subsystem: a central registration point for language reverse engineering (import) modules, and the reverse engineering methods common to all languages
persistence: Persistence: packages and unpackages the persistence data of the different subsystems to and from a storage medium (a flat .uml XML file or a zipped .zargo file); during save it collects each subsystem's data, during load it hands the data back to them
help: Help System: provides the menu actions that start the help and other documentation, and the infrastructure for context sensitive help (not yet implemented)
moduleLoader: Module loader, a View and Control subsystem: provides the mechanisms to load and unload the auxiliary modules; modules connect and register themselves to the subsystems they work with
gui: GUI framework, a View and Control subsystem: provides an infrastructure with menus, tool bars, tabs and panes for the other subsystems to fill with actions and contents; implemented directly on top of Swing, with no knowledge of UML, critics, diagrams or the model
model: Model, the Model subsystem (MVC): hides from the rest of ArgoUML which model repository is in use and gives a consistent interface for manipulating the data in it, including the important well-formedness rules
internationalization: Internationalization, a low-level subsystem: the infrastructure the other subsystems use to translate strings, to plug in new languages, and to administer the default and the supported languages
taskManagement: TaskManagement, a low-level subsystem: everything related to the concept of task, job or request, such as monitoring the progress of a long running task
configuration: Configuration, a low-level subsystem: stores and retrieves all configurable aspects of the application, kept in the user's home directory
swingExtensions: Swing extensions, a low-level subsystem: infrastructure for every other subsystem to use, depending on no other part of ArgoUML
ocl: OCL, a loadable subsystem: allows editing of strings in the OCL (Object Constraint Language), adapting an external OCL editor to ArgoUML
critics: Critics and other cognitive tools, a loadable subsystem: cognitive help for the user based on the current model: critics that find model elements not obeying simple design rules or best practices, checklists, wizards, and the to-do items they generate
javaCodeGeneration: Java, a loadable subsystem: converts the model into Java code and keeps it updated in Java or in the model, and converts Java code into a model (round-trip engineering for Java)
